text:
Tropical corn rust (Puccinia polysora).

Symptoms: small, round to oval, orange-brown pustules appear on both surfaces of the leaf, containing powdery spores that rub off easily on contact. Severe infection can cause leaves to dry out and senesce prematurely, reducing the plant's photosynthetic capacity and, in turn, yield.

Management: avoid overly dense planting and conditions that create excess shade or humidity, since these favour rust development; use resistant varieties where available; monitor fields regularly and apply fungicide if infection becomes severe; and use crop rotation and field sanitation to reduce carryover of disease inoculum between seasons.
